correctness.rationale: For arbitrary points in a triangle, the two support-line slopes at the perpendicular-bisector chord endpoints are bounded by the chord half-lengths. The smaller unoriented angle between the supporting side lines is at least the minimum triangle angle, so convexity of tangent gives \(C(T)\ge \tan(\alpha/2)\). The minimum-angle vertex and its internal angle-bisector foot attain equality. Splitting by acute versus obtuse largest angle then reduces \(r/R\) at fixed \(C(T)\) to a one-variable monotonicity calculation, yielding both sharp envelopes and equality families.
residual_risks: The radius R is the smallest-containing-disk radius, not always the ordinary circumcircle radius; the proof handles this with separate branches.
